contents_tesim: Usually only parts of lines are preserved, and only where the name of a saint is legible has it been possible to identify a specific underlying Greek canon. In such cases, it is clear that the translation is very free, and also different from that of the same canon which happens to be preserved in British Library manuscripts
full_text_tesim: British Library manuscripts consulted: Add. 14504, 9th c., Syrian Orthodox ; Add. 14505, 10th c., Syrian Orthodox ; Add. 12179, 11th-12th c., Melkite ; Add. 17236, dated 1234, Melkite
Melkite Estrangela | Neat and fairly regular; some serto features. The script is quite similar to that of Tropologion B, but usually rather neater
Not possible to discern the original order.

Sometimes part of a margin is present, top, right, left, or bottom (occasionally a combination of two of these). Blank spaces within or between lines probably had rubrics in different ink, which have left no trace in any of the images
The content (canons for feasts and saints' days) is evidently very similar to that of the UTO Tropologion B
UTO Sinai Syriac NF M 3, SPP No. 71

Usually only parts of lines are preserved, and only where the name of a saint is legible has it been possible to identify a specific underlying Greek canon. In such cases, it is clear that the translation is very free, and also different from that of the same canon which happens to be preserved in British Library manuscripts
